reader_summary.headline: Chris Hohn increased his Martin Marietta stake despite the stock trading far above its calculated value.
reader_summary.overview: Chris Hohn grew his position in Martin Marietta Materials by 37% and added more Vulcan Materials. This move happened even though the stock price was much higher than the calculated intrinsic value. The episode explains why paying a premium for quality matters when a portfolio relies on only twelve stocks.

key_points.text: Hohn increased his Martin Marietta stake by 37% with a $233.1 million buy.
key_points.evidence_quote: Chris Hohn grew his Martin Marietta Materials stake by 37%, a $233.1 million buy

key_points.text: The stock price of $507.07 is significantly higher than the base intrinsic value of $46.18.
key_points.evidence_quote: even though our base intrinsic value for Martin Marietta is $46.18 against a $507.07 price

key_points.text: Hohn also added 13% more Vulcan Materials to his holdings.

reader_summary.why_it_matters: Listeners learn why paying up for quality is important when a large portfolio rests on just twelve stocks.
